## Workshop 1 and 2: Spatial Visualisations of Mt Taranaki

``` bash
//2.10 Visualising data in Earth Engine
Map.setOptions('SATELLITE') //switches map view to satellite imagery
var snazzy = require("users/aazuspan/snazzy:styles");
snazzy.addStyle("https://snazzymaps.com/style/48750/blank-map", "Blank"); //enables a layout from snazzy maps
Map.setCenter(174.0638, -39.298, 11);// this sets the location to these specific coords, in this case mt taranaki
//lets add some elevation data
// Import SRTM data
var dataset = ee.Image("CGIAR/SRTM90_V4")
print (dataset) // Look at the data properties
// now add it to the map
////Map.addLayer(dataset)
// its flat gray now so lets do some visualisation
//Map.addLayer(dataset, {min: 0, max: 2500}, 'custom visualization');// second param is visual params it let’s you set the minimum pixel value and the maximum pixel values to display
//you can add more to the function to change its colouration and gradient
//Map.addLayer(dataset, {min: 0, max: 2500, palette: ['blue', 'green', 'red']},'custom palette');
// you can also choose to seperate the visParams from the function and run it seperately
// Set up visualisation parameters
var elevationVis = {
  min: 0,
  max: 2500,
  palette: ['0000ff', '00ffff', 'ffff00', 'ff0000', 'ffffff']
};

// Add the data layer to the map
//Map.addLayer(dataset, elevationVis, 'Elevation');
//using the inspector, mt taranaki is 2478m high and the SRTM data is an image, there is no data in the ocean as it is not part of the dataset

//now lets work with a vector dataset
// Add the protected planet data
var protected_areas = ee.FeatureCollection("WCMC/WDPA/current/polygons")
//lets add it to the map
//Map.addLayer(protected_areas)
//and add some color
//Map.addLayer(protected_areas, {color: 'yellow'}, 'Protected Areas')
// under the objects tab in the inspector it shows the data for every layer under the protected areas feature collections
//Egmont national park
//dept of conservation manages it
//designated National park

// lets find the number of protected areas
print ('No of protected areas:', protected_areas.size()) //307004
// lets select only features from cat 2 national parks under the IUCN_CAT property
print (protected_areas)
print (protected_areas.first()) // looking just at the first feature is much faster
print (protected_areas.limit(5)) // or we can look at a list of the first 5
// Filter only for level II protected areas
var iucn_pa = protected_areas.filter(ee.Filter.eq('IUCN_CAT', 'II'));
//Map.addLayer(iucn_pa, {color: 'lime'}, 'National Parks')

// filter date for 1980s
var iucn_pre1980 = protected_areas.filter(ee.Filter.lte('STATUS_YR', 1980));
//Map.addLayer(iucn_pre1980, {color: 'white'}, 'PAs in 1980');
print ('No of protected areas pre 1980s:', iucn_pre1980.size()) //64510
// filter date for greater than or equal to 2010s
var iucn_post2010 = protected_areas.filter(ee.Filter.gte('STATUS_YR', 2010));
//Map.addLayer(iucn_post2010, {color: 'brown'}, 'PAs in 2010 or more');

// lets do a spatial filter for protected areas in new zealand
// lets import a country dataset
var countries = ee.FeatureCollection("USDOS/LSIB_SIMPLE/2017");
print ('countries', countries); // look at it. // how to find a country name?
//Map.addLayer(countries,{color: 'grey'}, 'raw countries'); // look at it.
// New Zealand only
var nz = countries.filter(ee.Filter.equals('country_na', 'New Zealand'));
print (nz);
//Map.addLayer(nz); // look at it.

// Spatial filter PAs only in NZ
var nz_pas = protected_areas.filter(ee.Filter.bounds(nz))
print ('Number of PAs in NZ:', nz_pas.size())
//Map.addLayer(nz_pas, {color:'00FFAF'}, 'NZ PAs only')

// lets find cat 2 parks in NZ
// Link them all into one statement
var nz_national_parks = protected_areas
    .filter(ee.Filter.eq('IUCN_CAT', 'II')) // filter only NPs
    .filter(ee.Filter.bounds(nz)) // filter to NZ

print ('Number of National Parks in NZ:', nz_national_parks.size()) //18

//COMPUTATIONS IN EARTH ENGINE

// Change opacity
Map.addLayer(dataset, elevationVis, 'Elevation', true, 0.6);
print (dataset)

//lets add a constant
//Computation
print (dataset) 
var srtm_fixed = dataset.add(100)
Map.addLayer(srtm_fixed, elevationVis, 'fixed srtm')

//image thresholding for any pixel greater than 1500 elevation
var elevGt1500 = dataset.gt(1500) 
//Map.addLayer(elevGt1500) // Binary white == true

//use selfmask to exclude 0 values
var elevGt1500 = dataset.gt(1500).selfMask() 
//Map.addLayer(elevGt1500) 
Map.addLayer(elevGt1500.selfMask(), {palette:'fuchsia'}, 'gt 1500m', true, 0.7) 

//use the algorithm slope, from the terrain set of functions,  so that we can view just how steep the sides of Mt Taranaki are.
// apply complex algorithm
// Use terrain, an algorithm that returns several topographic variables from an elevation image
var terrain = ee.Terrain.products(dataset);
print ('terrain', terrain ) // print it to see what's inside

// make images from the bands we are interested in
var slope = terrain.select(['slope']) 
var hillshade = terrain.select(['hillshade'])
//Map.addLayer (hillshade)
//Map.addLayer (slope, {palette: ['white', 'darkred', 'black'], min:0, max:45}, 'slope')

//region reducers
//lets calculate avrg slope, max and min elevation and how much area above 1500m occurs inside the national park
// Find Taranaki NP
var taranaki = protected_areas.filter(ee.Filter.eq('NAME', 'Egmont National Park'));
Map.addLayer(taranaki, {color: 'orange'}, 'Mt Taranaki')

// Apply a spatial reducer to estimate mean slope
var slopeOutput = slope.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), // we compute the mean of all slope pixel values in the national park
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 // pixel size in metres - get this from the metadata (ie. search for it)
})
print ('slopeOutput', slopeOutput)// mean slope: 10.036223266342436

// Try clipping to see if it's any different.
var taranakiSlope = slope.clip(taranaki)
Map.addLayer (taranakiSlope, {palette: ['white', 'darkred', 'black'], min:0, max:45}, 'taranaki slope')

var slopeOutput2 = taranakiSlope.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), // we compute the mean of all slope pixel values in the national park
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 // pixel size in metres - get this from the metadata (ie. search for it)
})
print ('slopeOutput2', slopeOutput2) // same answer

// Use reduce regions with a different reducer (Max)
var elevOutput_Max = dataset.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.max(), // we compute the max of all pixel values in the national park
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 // pixel size in metres - get this from the metadata (ie. search for it)
})
print ('elevOutput_Max', elevOutput_Max) //elevation: 2484

// Use reduce regions with a different reducer (min)
var elevOutput_Min = dataset.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.min(), // we compute the min of all slope pixel values in the national park
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 // pixel size in metres - get this from the metadata (ie. search for it)
})
print ('elevOutput_Min', elevOutput_Min) //elevation: 108

// Use reduce regions with a different reducer
var elevOutput_MinMax = dataset.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.minMax(), // we compute both the min and max of all slope pixel values in the national park
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 // pixel size in metres - get this from the metadata (ie. search for it)
})
print ('elevOutput_MinMax', elevOutput_MinMax) // min 108 and max 2484

//  finding the area of the national park above our 1500m threshold
// Get area of >1500m
var areaGt1500m = elevGt1500 // binary 1 == yes
  .multiply (ee.Image.pixelArea()) // get the area of each pixel
  .reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), // sum all pixel areas together
  geometry: taranaki,
  scale:90 
})
print ('The area of Taranaki above 1500m (m2)', areaGt1500m) // in square metres 11474443.340820312
print ('The area of Taranaki above 1500m (km2)', ee.Number(areaGt1500m.get('elevation')).divide(1000 * 1000)) // in square kilometres 11.474443340820313

//WORLDCLIM
var datasetClim = ee.ImageCollection('WORLDCLIM/V1/MONTHLY');
print (datasetClim) // 12 images where each one is a month


// Get two months
var jan_climate = ee.Image ("WORLDCLIM/V1/MONTHLY/01")
var july_climate = ee.Image ("WORLDCLIM/V1/MONTHLY/07")


// Select their average temperature bands
var jan_climate_avg = jan_climate.select('tavg').multiply(0.1); // get average band
var july_climate_avg = july_climate.select('tavg').multiply(0.1);


// Set vis parameters
var meanTemperatureVis = {
  min: -40,
  max: 30,
  palette: ['blue', 'purple', 'cyan', 'green', 'yellow', 'red'],
};

Map.addLayer(jan_climate_avg, meanTemperatureVis, 'janClimate')
Map.addLayer(july_climate_avg, meanTemperatureVis, 'julyClimate')
// Inspect them!

// Note the pixel scaling error and fix it
// Need to divide all pixel values by 10, or multiply by .1 (.multiply(0.1)
// We want to reduce to get the yearly average
var annualMeanTemperature = datasetClim
  .select('tavg')
  .mean() // this is the reducer
  .multiply(0.1); // scale pixels to real values

Map.setCenter(71.7, 52.4, 3);
Map.addLayer(annualMeanTemperature, meanTemperatureVis, 'Mean Annual Temperature');

//import landsat imagery
var datasetLandsat = ee.ImageCollection('LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_TOA')
  .filterDate('2017-01-01', '2017-12-31'); // only images from 2017
var trueColour = datasetLandsat.select(['B4', 'B3', 'B2']);
var trueColourVis = {
  min: 0.0,
  max: 0.4,
};
Map.setCenter(146.746, -19.529, 9);
Map.addLayer(trueColour, trueColourVis, 'True Colour Landsat');

// Let's use reduce these
var LandsatMedian = trueColour.median()
Map.addLayer(LandsatMedian, trueColourVis, 'True Color Median');
```

## Workshop 2 Assignment : Map of Deep Ocean Marine Ecosystems

``` bash
//ASSIGNMENT 1 MODULE 4

Map.setOptions('SATELLITE') //switch map view to satellite imagery

// Import the ETOPO1 data
var etopoRaw = ee.Image("NOAA/NGDC/ETOPO1");
print('raw ETOPO1 properties', etopoRaw);
//Map.addLayer (etopoRaw)

// Select the bedrock band of this imagery
var bedrock = etopoRaw.select('bedrock');
//Map.addLayer (bedrock);

// thresholding for Hadal (>6000m)
var hadal = bedrock.lt(-6000).selfMask();

//thresholding for Abyssal Plains (3000-6000m)
var abyssal = bedrock.lte(-3000).and(bedrock.gte(-6000)).selfMask();

//thresholding for Continental Island Slopes (250-3000m)
var continentalIsland = bedrock.lte(-250).and(bedrock.gte(-3000)).selfMask();

//thresholding for Submarine Canyons (deeper than 200m, slopes of >6 degrees)
//but first we must find the slope
var terrain = ee.Terrain.products(bedrock);
print ('terrain', terrain ) // print it to see what's inside
var slope = terrain.select(['slope']) // this is slope
//Map.addLayer (slope, {palette: ['white', 'darkred', 'black'], min:0, max:45}, 'slope')
var hillshade = terrain.select(['hillshade']) // this is hillshade
//Map.addLayer (hillshade)
//now we threshold
var canyons = bedrock.lt(-3000).and(slope.gt(6)).selfMask();

// Add these variables as layers
var bedrockVis = {
  hadal: '40004b',
  abyssal: '0571b0',  
  continentalIsland: '92c5de',   
  canyons: 'f46d43',  
};//set the visual parameters

Map.addLayer(hadal, {palette:'bd0026'}, 'Hadal (>6000m)'); // add hadal layer
Map.addLayer(abyssal, {palette:'fd8d3c'}, 'Abyssal Plains (3000-6000m)'); // add abyssal plains layer
Map.addLayer(continentalIsland, {palette:'ffffcc'}, 'Continental Island Slopes (250-3000m)'); // add continental island slopes layer
Map.addLayer(canyons, {palette:'800026'}, 'Submarine Canyons (deeper than 200m, slopes of >6 degrees)'); // add submarine canyons layer

// Now lets add the vector dataset (protected areas, filtered to marine protected areas)
// // now add data on marine protected areas
var wdpa = ee.FeatureCollection("WCMC/WDPA/current/polygons")
print(wdpa)
print (wdpa.limit(5))// this didnt allow me to determine what the name of the REALM property was for mpas so i clicked on a known mpa (paravi dupatha or pigeon island national park in sri lanka) and found the realm name was 'Marine'
//Map.addLayer(wdpa, {color: 'cyan'}, 'Global Protected Areas')


// Filter for only Marine Protected Areas
var mpa = wdpa.filter(ee.Filter.eq('REALM', 'Marine'));
//add to map
Map.addLayer(mpa, {color: 'cyan'}, 'Marine Protected Areas')
```
